pages.text: CC:Tweaked's computers are built from chips, and chips come off a fab line of spouts, deployers, presses and saws.
pages.title: The Fab

pages.text: A wafer goes round once per mask layer: expose it through the mask a deployer holds, develop the resist, etch the oxide in hydrofluoric acid, dope or metallise the openings, grow fresh oxide in steam and coat resist for the next layer.

The microcontroller is 10 µm PMOS of 1971: an n-type wafer, three layers, negative rubber resist developed in naphtha, boron diffused in. Memory is 1 µm NMOS on p-type, five layers of positive novolac resist developed in caustic soda, phosphorus from its chloride.
The microprocessor is 1 µm CMOS on an epitaxial wafer, six layers, with aluminium interconnect.

The advanced processor is 90 nm: eight layers, copper interconnect polished flat by a press after each. Masks are chromium on glass, or on fused quartz for the reticles, etched in ceric ammonium nitrate.

A reticle's quartz is lapped flat first: a deployer holding garnet paper or emery cloth works it, wearing the paper, before the chromium goes on. The 90 nm reticle is laser-written by a computer, so better computers take a computer to make.

A saw dices each wafer into dies, more or fewer as the yield falls; each die goes onto a copper lead frame with gold bond wires and is sealed in plastic. A placed computer runs only beside a Power Supply on a live grid. It warms the air it runs in and trips its thermal cutout past 85 °C.
Turtles run on fuel, pocket computers on their cells.
